answer: To vote on dawn allocations of karst spring water to pearl farms, each AI key must reserve a certified secure chip for the day. Auction validators check unique chip certificates, fresh signatures and a one-chip/one-key registry; invalid or duplicate claims get no vote. Daily binding prevents time-sharing across keys, even on shared hosts. Chips are reusable capital, not fees or forfeited deposits; power costs recur. Corrupt manufacturers can certify fake devices, and wealth can buy aliases. With honest issuance, ten voting keys need ten chips, however signing is parallelized.
